title: Preventing Something: Para Que No and No Sea Que

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *para que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 4, and *para* + infinitive when one person acts, from B2 Unit 4. To say that the purpose is to avoid something, put *no* right after the connector: *Cierro la ventana para que no entre el frío* means "I close the window so that the cold does not come in." With one subject use an infinitive: *Hablo bajo para no despertar al bebé*. The tense rule is the same as before. There is one more pattern for precautions: *no sea que* + subjunctive, "in case". It comes after a command or a plan and warns about something that might happen: *Lleva un paraguas, no sea que llueva*.

sections.title: Purpose that avoids something
rows: a fin de que no + subjunctive
para no, a fin de no + infinitive

items.spanish: Cierra la puerta para que el gato no salga a la calle.
items.english: Close the door so that the cat does not go out into the street.

items.spanish: Anotamos la hora a fin de no llegar tarde.
items.english: We wrote down the time so as not to arrive late.

items.spanish: Anota el número, no sea que lo olvides.
items.english: Write the number down, in case you forget it.

items.spanish: Cerramos las ventanas a fin de que no entrara el frío.
items.english: We closed the windows so that the cold would not come in.

sections.content: Put *no* between the connector and the verb: *para que no salga*, *para no salir*. Keep the subjunctive after *no sea que*: say *no sea que llueva*, not *no sea que llueve*. *No sea que* is a warning about a possible problem rather than a plain purpose, so it has no infinitive form.
